sections.h2: Which jobs does the Cabarrus County Register of Deeds do for a seller?
sections.html:
It is the office that records your deed, your buyer's deed of trust and every release or assignment tied to the property, and it keeps them as public record. The county calls the register the legal custodian for recording, indexing, storing and preserving land documents, birth, death and marriage records, veteran discharges, notary records, subdivision maps and condominium plans.

Counter staff here only record. The county says state law bars them from practicing law, so no blank forms, no coaching on how to fill one in, and no opinion on what a signed instrument means for you. Drafting normally falls to your closing attorney.

Once recorded, every page becomes open to public viewing. The county warns against putting a Social Security number or bank account number on anything you submit.

sections.h2: Why does the recording time matter to a Cabarrus County seller?
sections.html:
Because the clock stamp decides priority. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance only protects the buyer against lien creditors and later purchasers for value once it is registered in the county where the land lies, and the order of registration sets who comes first. Because recording hours end at 4:30 p.m., ask the closing attorney when the package will reach the office.

Two practical points follow for a seller. Confirm that the payoff of your old mortgage has been released, because a satisfaction of a deed of trust carries no recording fee under state law, but it still has to be filed. Ask the closing attorney to check that every owner named on the deed signs and that the legal description matches your prior deed.

sections.h2: What are the filing hours in Cabarrus County, and what payment is accepted?
sections.html:
The window for filing is weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., and cash or a check is the only way to pay recording fees. The county says credit cards are not accepted for recording fees, which catches out sellers who expect to settle every charge by card at the counter.

After you bring or mail in a document, the office follows a fixed routine:

  • Staff check that the document can be recorded and work out the correct fee
  • It is stamped with the date and time, then given a document number, book and page
  • It is indexed in the computer system
  • Each day the documents are imaged, and a copy goes to the NC Department of Archives for backup
  • The processed document is returned to the proper party by the next day

That one-day return is worth knowing if a buyer's lender is waiting on proof of recording.

sections.h2: What fees apply when a deed is recorded in Cabarrus County?
sections.html:
A deed or other general instrument costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each page after that, while a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64 for the first 35 pages and $4 per added page. These match the uniform statewide fees in G.S. 161-10.

Recording fees on the Cabarrus County Register of Deeds fee page
DocumentFee
Deeds, trustee deeds, releases, assignments, powers of attorney$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Plats (mylar, 18 x 24 inches only)$21 per sheet
Subsequent instrument citing more than one original$10 for each added reference
Nonstandard document$25 on top of the recording fee

The $25 nonstandard fee applies when paper size, margins, ink or type fall short of G.S. 161-14. The county lists letter or legal paper, a three inch blank margin at the top of page one, one-sided black print and a font of at least 10 point. The fee does not apply to a document whose notary acknowledgement predates July 1, 2002.

sections.h2: How is the excise tax on a Cabarrus County deed collected?
sections.html:
The county's fee page says state law sets the stamp at $2 per $1,000 of the purchase price, collected with the recording fee, and that Cabarrus County and the State of NC split it equally. That agrees with G.S. 105-228.30, which charges one dollar per $500 of value or fraction and makes the transferor pay the register before recording.

Since the register takes only cash or check for recording fees, plan how the seller's side will be funded at the closing table. Most sellers have the closing attorney deduct the stamp from proceeds, so ask for the figure early and confirm who will deliver the payment to the office.

sections.h2: Can I search Cabarrus County property records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The register runs an online records search for property data, and the office's remote site holds indexes and document images from 1792 to the present, plus all subdivision plats, condominium plats and NC right-of-way maps. Cabarrus County was incorporated in 1792, so the record starts with the county itself.

The county partners with Logan Systems to redact Social Security and driver's license numbers from the internet copy, beginning with records from 1935. For older documents, the office has a Public Records Redaction Request form. The register files only fixture-related UCC statements, and everything else in that category goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

If a title search for your sale turns up an old lien or easement, the index is where a closing attorney will trace it.

sections.h2: What other services does the Cabarrus County office offer sellers?
sections.html:
The office handles a few side tasks that often come up around a sale or an estate. It files military discharges at no charge when you bring the original or a military copy with a raised seal, and only the person the statute allows may record or obtain a copy. Discharges that have been on file for 80 years or longer are public, while newer ones carry restricted access.

It also swears in new notaries, collecting a $10 oath fee, with no appointment needed once the Secretary of State's notice arrives. Copies of birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage license applications are available through the county's records pages, which helps heirs who need certificates to settle an inherited house.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about Cabarrus County itself?
sections.html:
Cabarrus County is a fast-growing Piedmont county north-east of Charlotte, with Concord as the county seat, about 18 miles from Charlotte and 124 miles from Raleigh. It covers roughly 230,400 acres and borders Rowan and Iredell counties to the north, Stanly to the east, Union to the south and Mecklenburg to the west.

The county budget document names the municipalities as Concord, Kannapolis, Mount Pleasant, Harrisburg, Midland and Locust. Its economy has moved from agriculture and textiles toward healthcare, manufacturing, warehousing, retail, motorsports and aviation. Atrium Health Cabarrus in Concord is the county's largest employer, Concord Mills draws around 17 million visitors a year, and Corning runs a large fiber optics plant in the southeast corner. The Grounds at Concord is a 2,100-acre industrial site where Eli Lilly and Red Bull have projects. Two school systems serve the county, Cabarrus County Schools and Kannapolis City Schools.

  • 249,725 residents in the July 2025 estimate, a 10.6% rise from the April 2020 base
  • Housing units on July 1, 2025: 100,316; owner-occupied rate 71.2% for 2020-2024
  • Typical owner-occupied home value of $354,800 in the 2020-2024 figures
  • Median gross rent for 2020-2024: $1,414; median household income $89,005
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,991; land area 361.23 square miles

faqs.q: What is the price of recording a deed with the Cabarrus County office?
faqs.a: A deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each extra page, per the county's fee page. Add the excise stamp, which the county lists at $2 per $1,000 of price, and a $25 nonstandard fee if the paper or print breaks the state format rules.

faqs.q: Will the Cabarrus County office take a card for recording fees?
faqs.a: No. The county says recording fees must be paid by cash or check and that credit cards are not accepted. Your closing attorney can usually handle the payment from the seller's proceeds.

faqs.q: What hours does Cabarrus County accept documents for recording?
faqs.a: Filing runs weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county says finished documents go back to the proper party by the next day.

faqs.q: Does the Cabarrus County Register of Deeds give legal advice on my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office acts as a recording office only, and North Carolina law prohibits staff from practicing law. They cannot supply legal forms, instruct you on completing them, or explain legal effects, so see an attorney.

faqs.q: How far back do Cabarrus County online records go?
faqs.a: The register's remote site has indexes and images from 1792 to the present, along with all subdivision plats, condominium plats and NC right-of-way maps. Redaction of personal numbers online begins with 1935 records, and older ones need a redaction request form.
